q: The Gottesman-Knill theorem states that quantum circuits consisting only of Clifford gates (Hadamard, CNOT, S gate) applied to computational basis states can be:
opts: Efficiently simulated by classical computers in polynomial time
Simulated classically only for n ≤ 50 qubits
exp: Gottesman-Knill: Clifford circuits are classically efficiently simulable. The stabilizer group (n Pauli operators) evolves under Clifford gates and can be tracked in O(n²) classical space. Clifford circuits are not universal—T gates (non-Clifford) are needed for universality.
